arml-local-2011-individual-01.title: Where is the median?
arml-local-2011-individual-01.body:
The median is $2$, $11$ or $x$ depending on whether $x<2$, $x>11$, or $2\le x\le11$. If $x\ge2$ the median is at most $11$ but the mean is $\frac{2024+x}5>404$, so they cannot be equal. Hence $x<2$, the median is $2$, and $\frac{2024+x}5=2$ gives $x=-2014$.

**Answer: $-2014$**

arml-local-2011-individual-02.title: Two equations
arml-local-2011-individual-02.body:
Let the fraction be $\frac AB$. $\frac{A+4}{B+4}=\frac35$ gives $5A+20=3B+12$; $\frac{A+1}{B+1}=\frac12$ gives $2A+2=B+1$, so $B=2A+1$. Then $5A+8=6A+3$ and $A=5$, $B=11$.

**Answer: $\dfrac5{11}$**

arml-local-2011-individual-04.title: Sum of angles
arml-local-2011-individual-04.body:
The angle sum of an $n$-gon is $180(n-2)$. An arithmetic progression with $n$ terms, first $130$ and last $170$, sums to $\frac{130+170}2n=150n$. So $150n=180n-360$ and $n=12$.

**Answer: 12**

arml-local-2011-individual-06.title: Binomial theorem
arml-local-2011-individual-06.body:
The general term is $\binom6p(3x^2)^{6-p}\left(\frac2x\right)^p$ with power of $x$ equal to $2(6-p)-p=12-3p$, which is $0$ for $p=4$. The term is $\binom64(3x^2)^2\left(\frac2x\right)^4=15\cdot9\cdot16=2160$.

**Answer: 2160**

arml-local-2011-individual-07.title: Last two digits
arml-local-2011-individual-07.body:
For $n\ge10$, $n!$ is a multiple of $100$. So only $1!,\dots,9!$ matter modulo $100$: $1+2+6+24+20+20+40+20+80=213$ (using $5!=120$, $6!=720$, $7!=5040$, $8!=40320$, $9!=362880$ mod $100$). The last two digits are $13$, so the tens digit is $1$.

**Answer: 1**

arml-local-2011-individual-08.title: Symmetry and the Pythagorean theorem
arml-local-2011-individual-08.body:
By symmetry about the diagonal $AC$, $BE=DF=t$ and $EC=FC=1-t$. Then $AE^2=1+t^2$ and $EF^2=2(1-t)^2$. Setting equal: $1+t^2=2-4t+2t^2$, so $t^2-4t+1=0$ and $t=2-\sqrt3$. $AE^2=1+(7-4\sqrt3)=8-4\sqrt3=(\sqrt6-\sqrt2)^2$.

**Answer: $\sqrt6-\sqrt2$**

arml-local-2011-individual-09.title: Work backwards
arml-local-2011-individual-09.body:
$b(b(b(n)))\ge2$ requires $b(b(n))\ge3$ (the smallest number with binary digit sum $\ge2$ is $3$), which requires $b(n)\ge7$ (the smallest number with digit sum $\ge3$ is $7$), which requires $n\ge127=1111111_2$ (the smallest number with digit sum $\ge7$). Check: $b(127)=7$, $b(7)=3$, $b(3)=2>1$.

**Answer: 127**

arml-local-2011-individual-10.title: Conjugate trick
arml-local-2011-individual-10.body:
$(\sqrt5+\sqrt3)^2=8+2\sqrt{15}$, so $(\sqrt5+\sqrt3)^4=124+32\sqrt{15}$ and $(\sqrt5-\sqrt3)^4=124-32\sqrt{15}$. The sum is the integer $248$. Since $0<\sqrt5-\sqrt3<1$, $0<(\sqrt5-\sqrt3)^4<1$, hence $(\sqrt5+\sqrt3)^4=248-\varepsilon$ with $0<\varepsilon<1$, and the ceiling is $248$.

**Answer: 248**

arml-local-2011-individual-11.title: Chord lengths
arml-local-2011-individual-11.body:
Let $R$ be the circumradius. A chord spanning $k$ sides has length $2R\sin\frac{k\pi}9$. So $AE=2R\sin80^\circ$, $AC=2R\sin40^\circ$ and the side is $2R\sin20^\circ=3$. Then $AE-AC=2R(\sin80^\circ-\sin40^\circ)=2R\cdot2\cos60^\circ\sin20^\circ=2R\sin20^\circ=3$.

**Answer: 3**

arml-local-2011-individual-11.title: Equilateral triangles
arml-local-2011-individual-11.body:
The interior angles of the nonagon are $140^\circ$. Extend $AC$ and $FD$ to meet at $J$. Angle chasing gives $\angle FDE=20^\circ$ and $\angle FDC=120^\circ$, so $\angle JDC=60^\circ$ and triangles $AFJ$ and $JDC$ are equilateral. Since $AF=AE$ (symmetry), $AE=AF=AJ=AC+CJ=AC+CD$, so $AE-AC=CD=3$.

**Answer: 3**
